endpoints.name: St George
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/1069480257 power=substation name='Saint George Switching Station' voltage=230000 substation=switching (no operator tag). Re-checked with the bulk export within 8 km of St. George (Nominatim relation/194006, 33.18600,-80.57565): it is the only 230 kV feature; the others are unnamed 115 kV substations.
endpoints.validation: The name matches and 230 kV matches '230kV Tie'. It is in St. George, Dorchester County, in DESC territory. NRC V.C. Summer FSAR Table 8.1-1 (nrc-vcsummer-fsar-ch8-rev22 p10) lists the SCE&G St. George to Duke Energy-Progress Sumter 230 kV tie. OSM topology agrees: 230 kV way/185032931 does not apply; way/185032932 (31.9 km) runs from this switching station to the unnamed Santee 230/115/46 kV substation, way/185032933 (42.2 km) continues to a junction at 33.8114,-80.3647, and double-circuit way/185032969 (11.6 km) ends at Sumter Substation. That is one continuous 230 kV St George-Santee-Sumter path.

endpoints.name: Sumter
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185032893 power=substation name='Sumter Substation' voltage=230000 substation=transmission (no operator tag)
endpoints.validation: The name matches and it is 230 kV. This is the Duke Energy-Progress end of the tie named in FSAR Table 8.1-1. It is the terminus of the 230 kV path from St George through Santee (see above). The same double-circuit entry also carries DESC's Wateree-Sumter tie (way/185032894), which matches the FSAR's 'Wateree - Sumter 230'. Sumter Industrial Substation (115 kV) is a false match.

projects.notes: The work scope is the segment from Santee Substation to the Duke/Progress tie. In OSM, DESC's Santee Substation is the unnamed 230/115/46 kV way/185032971 (33.46287,-80.46821); it is lower-confidence. Topology supports it: the St George-Sumter 230 kV line passes through it, and it is the origin of the 46 kV line way/12139895 to Santee City, Elloree, Cameron Jct and St Matthews. The rebuilt segment therefore lies on 230 kV way/185032933, which runs north from Santee (33.4624,-80.4677) toward the junction at 33.8114,-80.3647 where the Wateree-Sumter tie merges. The exact ownership/tie point was not found. The St George-Sumter midpoint (33.5485,-80.4580) is about 1.5 km off that segment, so it is a reasonable center for this work. KEY COLLISION: the 2026-2030 SCRTP uses Project ID '6809 M' twice, on p19 (this project) and on p48 ('Modoc - McCormick 115/46 kV Rebuild', batch desc-3). Both batches use the key 'desc:6809 M', so a key-based merge will overwrite one of them.

endpoints.name: Hooks
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/1074904615 power=substation name='GPC <-> SCG&E Compensator Station' substation=compensation voltage=115000, at the start of Hooks Road (Nominatim way/12471625, McCormick County SC). Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) line topology: SCG&E 115 kV way/1074904614 (1.0 km) runs east to the Stevens Creek-McCormick 115 kV (way/12356976) and 46 kV (way/1073388048) corridor at tower node/9858857049 (33.65557,-82.14901); Georgia Power 115 kV way/1074904617 (3.4 km) runs west to Thurmond Substation.
endpoints.validation: No OSM or public feature is named Hooks. This station is on Hooks Road at the SCE&G/GPC ownership change on the Hooks-Thurmond tie, which fits the name, but the name itself is not confirmed. Plan mileages leave about 1 km of ambiguity. Measured along OSM lines from Stevens Creek Dam Substation, the corridor junction is 8.85 mi and this station is 9.47 mi (plan 2024-2028 p14, 6809 E: Stevens Creek-Hooks 9.5 mi). From the junction to Modoc is 6.38 mi, and from this station 7.0 mi (plan: Hooks-Modoc 6.5 mi). To Thurmond it is 2.1 mi from this station and 2.7 mi from the junction (plan 6810 A: about 2.3 mi). Hooks is therefore this station or the corridor junction 0.98 km east. The 1000 m uncertainty covers both. The earlier title of this project was 'Stevens Creek - Hooks 115kV/LR Plumb Branch 46kV' (2024-2028 plan), which confirms it is on this corridor.

endpoints.name: Modoc
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/1074904620 power=substation name='Modoc Substation' voltage=46000; connected by way/1074904619 (0.1 km) to the Stevens Creek-McCormick 115/46 kV corridor (ways 12356976 and 1073388048)
endpoints.validation: The name matches and 46 kV matches '115/46 kV'. It is in Modoc, McCormick County SC, in DESC territory, and it is the only Modoc in SC and GA. It sits on the same SPDC 115/46 kV corridor as Hooks, 6.4 mi along the line from the Hooks junction, against the plan's 6.5 mi.

projects.notes: This work is at the state line. The Hooks area is 3.4 km from Georgia Power's Thurmond Substation and J. Strom Thurmond Dam, so it is highly relevant for GPC proximity. The Stevens Creek-McCormick corridor also hosts desc:6809 M (p48, Modoc-McCormick).

endpoints.name: Burton
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185362029 power=substation name='Burton Substation' operator='South Carolina Electric & Gas Company' voltage=230000
endpoints.validation: The name matches, the operator is SCE&G (DESC), and it is in Burton, Beaufort County. OSM 'Yemassee - Burton 230kV' and 'Burton - Yemassee 115kV' lines terminate here. The Georgia Power Burton Substation/Dam in Rabun County GA is a false match.

endpoints.name: St Helena
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/1064802547 power=substation (unnamed) operator='South Carolina Electric & Gas' voltage=115000, on Seaside Road, St. Helena Island. Overpass topology: it is the eastern terminus of 115 kV way/1064802539 (18.1 km), which passes the Frogmore Substation tap (way/1064802544).
endpoints.validation: This unnamed SCE&G 115 kV substation is the end of the only 115 kV line on St. Helena Island, 7.3 km past Frogmore. That matches the Burton-Frogmore-St Helena order in the plan. No source names it St Helena, so the match rests on operator, voltage, position and topology.

projects.notes: The rebuilt section is Frogmore to St. Helena. Frogmore Substation is OSM way/1064802545 (SCE&G, 115/23 kV) at 32.39913,-80.57113, a named and confirmed match. A center based on that section would be about 32.406,-80.533.

endpoints.name: Tap point on Edmund Switching Station - Owens Corning 115 kV line
endpoints.coordinateSource: Digitized from the DESC 'Future Wagener 115 kV Tap Selected Route Corridor' map (July 2025; cached as desc-wagener-selected-route-map, p1). The map shows the NW end of the new route meeting the 'Existing 115kV Transmission Line' near Koala Bear Rd. The map was georeferenced from the Pinder Pl/SC 39 junction (OSM way/12098633) using the map's 10,000 ft scale bar. The digitized point falls 31 m from OSM 115 kV way/185404030, which runs from 33.8623,-81.1842 (about 2 km from the Edmund Substation, way/552694024) southwest to 33.6002,-81.5737.
endpoints.validation: The DESC map is an official public source, but it labels the line only as 'Existing 115kV'. That this is the Edmund-Owens Corning line comes from the SCRTP description and from OSM way/185404030 running from the Edmund area toward Aiken. Koala Bear Road (Nominatim 33.69861,-81.44070) agrees with the map. The point depends on hand digitizing, so the uncertainty is 500 m.

endpoints.name: Wagener Distribution substation (new)
endpoints.coordinateSource: Digitized from the DESC Selected Route Map (desc-wagener-selected-route-map p1; excerpt 'Future Wagener Distribution Substation' verified with find_excerpt). The site is on the east side of Pinder Place (OSM way/12098633), about 0.47 km north of SC 39 / Old Ninety Six Indian Trail. Georeferenced from the Pinder Pl/SC 39 junction (33.66258,-81.39151) and the 10,000 ft scale bar.
endpoints.validation: The DESC route notification letter of July 30, 2025 (cached as desc-wagener-tap-route-notification p1; 'a new substation northwest of Wagener' verified) and the route map both name this new substation. It is 3.0 km WNW of the Wagener town centroid, which agrees with 'northwest of Wagener'. The existing 46 kV OSM 'Wagener Substation' (way/993540535) is 3.2 km away, in town, and is not the new site.

projects.notes: The kind was changed from 'other' to 'line' because the project is a 115 kV tap line with two terminals shown on DESC's own route map. The center is the midpoint, about 33.681,-81.418. The straight-line length is 3.96 mi and the mapped route is about 4.2 mi. The DESC 'Wagener Connection' page (cached as desc-wagener-connection-page) describes 'a new approximately 6.5-mile 115-kilovolt (kV) line'. That length discrepancy is unresolved. The same page gives 'Construction ... will begin in early 2028 and is scheduled to finish by year's end', which conflicts with the SCRTP 2026-2030 in-service date of 12/31/27. Keep both claims as a source conflict. The page gives a construction window, not only an in-service date.

endpoints.name: Cameron Jct
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM node/5211620240 power=pole line_management=branch, where 46 kV way/623292013 (from the Orangeburg East complex) joins the Santee-Elloree-Cameron-St Matthews 46 kV line way/12139895. Found with Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) line queries.
endpoints.validation: No name is tagged in OSM, but three independent plan mileages match this branch pole when measured along OSM line geometry. Cameron Jct to the Elloree tap is 7.31 mi (plan 6810 U: 7.3 mi). Cameron Jct to St Matthews 46 kV substation (way/1077428670) is 9.9 mi (plan 6810 T: 9.8 mi). Cameron Jct to the Orangeburg East complex is 7.81 mi (plan 6809 F: 7.5 mi). The pole is 1.3 mi along the line before Cameron Substation (way/318318141) and 2.0 km from the Cameron town centroid. The earlier locality point was replaced.

endpoints.name: Elloree
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/1075509549 power=substation name='Elloree Substation' voltage=46000; fed by 1.3 km 46 kV tap way/1077428678 from 33.52795,-80.59141 on way/12139895
endpoints.validation: The name matches, 46 kV matches, and it is in Elloree, Orangeburg County. It is the only Elloree. The line section ends at the tap point 0.7 mi from the substation, and the plan's 7.3 mi matches the distance to that tap point.

endpoints.name: Atomic Road 115/12kV Sub (new)
endpoints.coordinateSource: Center of the bounding box of the OSM highway ways named 'Atomic Road' (SC 125, Aiken County), 33.30875-33.49535 N, -81.95728 to -81.76197 W. Re-checked with Nominatim: the road runs from North Augusta (33.4913,-81.9543) through Clearwater and Beech Island (33.3969,-81.8466) to Jackson (33.3347,-81.7870).
endpoints.validation: This is a new customer-driven substation whose site is not published. Web searches found no 'Atomic Road Substation' filing or page. Only the road corridor is certain; it is about 27 km long and lies entirely within about 15 km of the Savannah River and the Georgia line. The uncertainty is larger than the usual 5-8 km for a locality because this is a road corridor, not a town.

projects.notes: This project is relevant to the GPC Augusta area (zone 215). The point should not be read as a precise site.

endpoints.name: Elloree
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/1075509549 power=substation name='Elloree Substation' voltage=46000
endpoints.validation: The name matches, 46 kV matches, and it is in Elloree, Orangeburg County.

endpoints.name: Santee City
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/1038600584 power=substation (unnamed) voltage=46000 substation=distribution, on Rebecca Street in Santee (Orangeburg County). It lies on 46 kV way/12139895, 1.74 mi from the Santee 230/115/46 kV substation (way/185032971).
endpoints.validation: This is the only 46 kV distribution substation in Santee town, 0.3 km from the centroid, and it sits on the Elloree-Santee 46 kV line. Along-line distances do not settle the match. From the Elloree tap it is 7.13 mi (7.94 mi including the Elloree tap). The alternative, the unnamed transmission substation way/185032971 2.1 km SE, is 8.87 mi (9.67 mi). The plan gives 8.35 mi. DESC calls that transmission site 'Santee Substation' in 6809 M, which argues that 'Santee City' is a separate facility, but the feature is unnamed and the match is unconfirmed.

endpoints.name: Urquhart
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM relation/14317637 power=substation name='Urquhart Substation' voltage=230000; adjacent OSM way/449466234 power=plant name='Urquhart Station' operator='Dominion Energy South Carolina, Inc'; 46 kV lines way/1041994615 and way/380872162 start at the complex (33.4329,-81.9103)
endpoints.validation: The name matches, and it sits beside DESC's Urquhart Station in Beech Island, Aiken County. OSM tags only 230 kV on the substation, but the 46 kV lines leave from the complex.

endpoints.name: Aiken PSA
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/1073388000 power=substation name='Beech Island Wastewater Substation' voltage=46000 substation=industrial, on 'Psa Road' (Nominatim way/12100661, 33.46950,-81.91287). It is fed by 46 kV tap way/1073388001 (0.9 km) from 33.47663,-81.90564 on 46 kV way/1073388002.
endpoints.validation: 'Aiken PSA' is the Aiken County Public Service Authority. This 46 kV wastewater substation is on PSA Road. The plan's own mileage confirms the tap: along OSM 46 kV lines from Urquhart (way/1041994615, then way/1073388002), the tap point at 33.47663,-81.90564 is 4.39 mi out, against the plan's 'Urquhart to the Aiken PSA tap point ... 4.5 miles'. The substation is 0.54 mi beyond the tap point, and the plan leaves open ('TBD') whether that tap is in scope.

projects.notes: The rebuilt section ends at the tap point, 33.47663,-81.90564, which is 0.8 km from the PSA substation. The project is directly across the Savannah River from Augusta. Georgia Power substations such as PCS Nitrogen and South Augusta are 1-6 km away, so it is highly relevant for GPC proximity.

endpoints.name: Wateree
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/1082130490 power=substation name='Wateree Substation' voltage=230000; adjacent OSM relation/17131066 power=plant name='Wateree Station' operator='Dominion Energy South Carolina, Inc'
endpoints.validation: The name matches and 230 kV matches. It sits beside DESC Wateree Station near Eastover, Richland County. The Duke 'Wateree Dam' substation is a false match.

endpoints.name: Hopkins
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185227970 power=substation (unnamed) voltage=230000;115000 substation=transmission; SC PSC Docket 2005-58-E order (scpsc-2005-58-e-hopkins-order p3). Overpass topology: two 230 kV paths from Wateree Substation end here, way/185225300 then way/769275562, and way/185227953 then way/185227983.
endpoints.validation: The PSC order names the 'Hopkins 230/115 kV Substation' on Westinghouse Electric Company property off Bluff Road. This OSM 230/115 kV substation is 0.72 km from the Westinghouse Columbia Fuel Fabrication Facility (OSM way/693429431, Nominatim 33.88263,-80.91795), and both Wateree 230 kV lines (#1 and #2) end at it.

endpoints.name: Adams Run
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/697675375 power=substation name='Adams Run Substation' voltage=115000
endpoints.validation: The name matches and it is in Adams Run, Charleston County, in DESC territory. OSM tags the 115 kV side, and the subtransmission line to Edisto starts here.

endpoints.name: Red House Road
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/446242261 power=substation name='Edisto Island Substation' voltage=69000, on Red House Road, Edisto Island (Nominatim reverse). Overpass topology: line way/1065036695 (tagged 69 kV, 26.4 km) runs from Adams Run Substation to this substation across the Dawhoo River.
endpoints.validation: Topology supports the site: the only line leaving Adams Run toward Edisto ends at this substation on Red House Road. A length of 16.4 mi and structure numbers up to 302 in the plan give spans of about 290 ft, which is plausible for this line. The OSM name ('Edisto Island') and voltage tags (69 kV on both line and substation) disagree with the plan's 'Red House Road' and 46 kV, so the match stays lower-confidence.

projects.notes: The Dawhoo River crossing lies between the endpoints. The midpoint, about 32.629,-80.324, is close to the crossing.

endpoints.name: Lyles
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185230443 power=substation (unnamed) voltage=230000;115000;33000 substation=transmission, at Columbia Riverfront/Canal; SC PSC Docket 2014-86-E order (scpsc-2014-86-e-lyles-order p6)
endpoints.validation: The PSC order describes the 'existing Lyles 230/115 kV Substation in Columbia' and mentions a lattice tower in the Columbia Canal near the Lyles Substation (verified with find_excerpt). This is the only 230/115 kV substation in central Columbia and it sits at the Canal/Riverfront. NRC FSAR Table 8.1-1 lists Lyles 115 kV ties.

endpoints.name: Kilbourne Park
endpoints.coordinateSource: Nominatim 'Kilbourne Park, Columbia, South Carolina' -> Kilbourne Park Church, Kilbourne Road, Heathwood, Columbia (way/370060881). Used only as a proxy for the Kilbourne Road area.
endpoints.validation: No OSM feature or public source names this substation. Two unnamed 115 kV candidates are within 2.5 km: way/528218922 (34.00889,-80.97025, mid-line on 115 kV way/1078487443) and way/554650082 (33.98727,-80.98606, terminus of 115 kV way/1078487460). A 115 kV path trace from Lyles did not reproduce the plan's 2.85 mi 'Richland Mall GOAB to Kilbourne Park' section for either candidate, so neither is confirmed. The work is in east Columbia near Forest Dr, N Beltline Blvd and Kilbourne Rd.

endpoints.name: Winnsboro West (new 230-115 kV substation)
endpoints.coordinateSource: Nominatim 'Winnsboro, South Carolina' relation/194076 (Fairfield County), re-verified
endpoints.validation: The SC PSC Docket 2025-208-E directive (scpsc-2025-208-e-winnsboro-west-directive p1) confirms the planned Winnsboro West Substation, the fold-in of the Parr-Winnsboro 115 kV #1 and VCS1-Killian 230 kV lines, and completion by January 31, 2028. It gives no site, and web searches found no public site map. NRC FSAR ch.8 p25 places the shared SPDC section of those two lines on the 13 miles from Winnsboro Junction (near VCS) to Winnsboro. The name points to the Winnsboro (east) end, but the site could be anywhere on that corridor.

projects.notes: The PSC directive gives expected completion as January 31, 2028.

endpoints.name: Williams
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/184867924 power=substation name='Williams Substation' voltage=230000;115000; adjacent OSM relation/20086234 power=plant name='Williams Station' operator='South Carolina Generating Company'
endpoints.validation: The name matches and 230 kV matches. It sits beside DESC's Williams Station in Goose Creek, Berkeley County.

endpoints.name: Summerville
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185236364 power=substation (unnamed) voltage=230000;115000 substation=transmission. Overpass topology: 230 kV from Williams runs way/184867944 or 184867945 (10.4 km), then way/184867946 (1.1 km), then way/1065709104 or 1065709105 (5.0 km) to a branch at 32.9884,-80.0940, then double-circuit way/184867928 (6.0 km) into this substation. The DESC St George-Summerville double-circuit 230 kV line (way/1069480265, 47.4 km) also ends here.
endpoints.validation: This is the only 230/115 kV substation within 10 km of Summerville. It is the terminus of a continuous 230 kV path from Williams (about 14.2 mi along OSM lines) and of the 230 kV line from DESC's St George switching station, so it is a DESC hub. The feature is unnamed in OSM. The Georgia 'Summerville Substation' is a false match.

projects.notes: The scope is Ladson Jct to Williams. A Ladson Jct candidate is the OSM branch at 32.9884,-80.0940, where 230 kV way/184867943 leaves toward Pepperhill. It is 10.3 mi along the line from Williams, matching the plan's 'Approximately 10 miles', and 2.45 km SSE of the Ladson CDP centroid. That candidate is lower-confidence (unnamed). A work-area center would be about 33.003,-80.013, about 3 km from the Williams-Summerville midpoint.

endpoints.name: Church Creek
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185330726 power=substation name='Church Creek Substation' voltage=230000;115000
endpoints.validation: The name matches and 230 kV matches. It is in West Ashley, Charleston County, in DESC territory, and it is the origin of the 56.0 km 230 kV line way/185397983 to Ritter.

endpoints.name: Ritter
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185397978 power=substation (unnamed) voltage=230000;115000 substation=transmission, 3.8 km north of Ritter hamlet (Nominatim 32.78962,-80.63038). Overpass topology: 230 kV way/185397983 (56.0 km) from Church Creek and 230 kV way/185399954 (27.5 km) from Yemassee (32.6983,-80.8633) both end here, and 115 kV way/1065036692 runs back toward Charleston.
endpoints.validation: This is the only 230 kV substation within 15 km of Ritter, Colleton County. It is the meeting point of the Church Creek-Ritter and Yemassee-Ritter 230 kV lines, which matches the plan's 'Yemassee - Ritter 230kV' (2026-2030 p17). The DESC Ritter-Yemassee page (cached) puts that corridor in Colleton and Hampton counties. The feature is unnamed in OSM.

endpoints.name: Jackson (new 115-12 kV sub replacing Jackson 46 kV)
endpoints.coordinateSource: Nominatim 'Jackson, South Carolina' relation/193856 (Aiken County), re-verified
endpoints.validation: The plan's 'Aiken Schools' customer ties this to Jackson in Aiken County, not Jackson in Georgetown County or Georgia Power's Jackson Substation in Butts County GA. The site of the new 115 kV substation is not published. An unnamed OSM substation, way/1493721095 at 33.33399,-81.78704 on Atomic Road (no voltage tag), may be the existing Jackson 46 kV station. That is unconfirmed.

projects.notes: This site is about 17 km from the Savannah River and the Georgia line.

endpoints.name: Blue Circle tap
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/1075801494 power=substation name='Argos Substation' voltage=115000 substation=industrial (Harleyville cement plant); it is the terminus of 115 kV tap way/1075801493 (3.6 km) from 33.2333,-80.4876 on 115 kV way/1075801492
endpoints.validation: Public reporting found via web search (Post and Courier, cemnet, GEM wiki) gives the plant's ownership as Gifford-Hill (1974), then Blue Circle, then Lafarge (2001), then Argos (2011). This 115 kV industrial substation is the end of the existing 115 kV tap to that plant, i.e. the 'Blue Circle tap'. It is 1.0 mi straight-line from Harleyville Substation, against the plan's 1.4 mi extension. The exact start of the extension may be offset from the plant substation.

endpoints.name: Harleyville
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/1075801506 power=substation name='Harleyville Substation' voltage=46000
endpoints.validation: The name matches and it is in Harleyville, Dorchester County. It is currently 46 kV, which fits the plan's aim to 'provide 115 kV service'.

endpoints.name: Orangeburg #1
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185577980 power=substation (unnamed) voltage=115000 substation=distribution, inside the DESC Orangeburg East complex (Orangeburg East Substation way/185577981 is 230/115 kV; the OSM line 'Orangeburg East - St. George 115kV #1' leaves it). It is the west terminus of 46 kV way/623292013 (7.81 mi), which runs to the Cameron Jct branch pole node/5211620240.
endpoints.validation: This is the only 46 kV line that reaches Cameron Jct from the west, and its 7.81 mi length matches the plan's '7.5 mile Orangeburg #1 - Cameron Jct.' It ends at this substation on the east side of Orangeburg, 4.6 km east of the city centroid. No source uses the name 'Orangeburg #1' for this feature, and its OSM voltage tag is 115 kV only, so the match is lower-confidence. It replaces the earlier city-centroid locality.

endpoints.name: Cameron Jct
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM node/5211620240 power=pole line_management=branch, the junction of 46 kV way/623292013 and way/12139895
endpoints.validation: This is the same point as in desc:6810 U. Three plan mileages match it along OSM lines: 7.3 mi to the Elloree tap (7.31 measured), 9.8 mi to St Matthews (9.9) and 7.5 mi to Orangeburg #1 (7.81).

projects.notes: The 2025-2029 plan's description for 6809 F reads 'Calhoun County - St Matthews 46 kV Line' under the same title. That looks like a copy error in the source; the 2026-2030 text is used here.

endpoints.name: VCS1
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185039621 power=substation name='Virgil C. Summer Nuclear #1 Substation' voltage=230000
endpoints.validation: VCS1 is the V.C. Summer Unit 1 switchyard in Jenkinsville, Fairfield County, at 230 kV. NRC FSAR ch.8 names the VCS1-Denny Terrace and VCS1-Pineland 230 kV lines.

endpoints.name: Denny Terrace
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185130609 power=substation name='Denny Terrace Substation' operator='South Carolina Electric & Gas Company' voltage=230000
endpoints.validation: The name, SCE&G operator and 230 kV all match. The SC PSC 2010-238-E application (scpsc-2010-238-e-pineland-application p5, verified) places it in Northeast Columbia near Peeples St and Brickyard Rd.

endpoints.name: Pineland
endpoints.coordinateSource: OSM way/185130617 power=substation (unnamed) voltage=230000 substation=transmission; Nominatim reverse -> Pisgah Church Road; SC PSC Docket 2010-238-E application p5
endpoints.validation: The PSC application (verified with find_excerpt) places the Pineland Transmission Substation in Northeast Columbia near Pisgah Church Road and Wilson Boulevard (US 21). This 230 kV substation is 0.2 km from Pisgah Church Road. The 69 kV 'Pineland Substation' in Jasper County is a false match.

projects.notes: There are three terminals because two lines share VCS1. NRC FSAR ch.8 (pp23-24) says both lines run on double-circuit structures for the first 17.24 mi from VCS. The single-circuit wood H-frame sections being rebuilt are the Columbia-end spans: about 6.6 mi into Pineland and about 7.5-9 mi into Denny Terrace. A work-area center is about 34.081,-81.022.

unresolved: desc:6809 M: the Duke/Progress tie (ownership) point on the Santee-Sumter 230 kV segment was not located. The DESC Santee Substation is known only as unnamed OSM way/185032971 (lower-confidence, supported by topology).

desc:6809 M key collision: the 2026-2030 SCRTP uses Project ID '6809 M' on p19 (St George-Sumter, batch desc-2) and on p48 (Modoc-McCormick, batch desc-3). Both batches emit the key 'desc:6809 M'; the pipeline needs a page-qualified key (for example 'desc:6809 M@p19').

desc:6809 G: Hooks is within about 1 km: either the 'GPC <-> SCG&E Compensator Station' on Hooks Road or the corridor junction tower node/9858857049 0.98 km east. The plan mileages do not decide between them.
desc:6388 A: Ladson Jct is given only as a lower-confidence topology candidate (32.9884,-80.0940) in notes.
desc:7956B: the Atomic Road substation site is not published. Only the 27 km Atomic Road (SC 125) corridor is known, so the uncertainty is 14 km.
desc:6873: the Winnsboro West substation site is not published. It lies on the 13-mile VCS1-Killian / Parr-Winnsboro #1 SPDC corridor; a Winnsboro locality is used.

desc:06371 D: the DESC Wagener Connection page gives about 6.5 mi, but the mapped tap route measures about 4.2 mi. The page's 2028 construction window also conflicts with the SCRTP in-service date of 12/31/27. Both should be kept as source conflicts.
issuesFixed: desc:06371 D: I replaced the Wagener town-centroid locality (5000 m) with the actual future substation site from DESC's own Selected Route Map (July 2025): 33.6668,-81.3884, named-facility, 500 m, confirmed, about 3.0 km WNW of the town. I changed kind from 'other' to 'line' and added the tap-point terminal on the Edmund-Owens Corning 115 kV line (33.6953,-81.4481, lower-confidence). That point was digitized from the same map and falls within 31 m of OSM 115 kV way/185404030. I cached three new DESC sources with fetch_source.py and verified excerpts with find_excerpt.py: desc-wagener-selected-route-map, desc-wagener-tap-route-notification ('a new substation northwest of Wagener', p1) and desc-wagener-connection-page (construction early 2028 to end of 2028, about 6.5 mi). The date and length conflicts are listed under unresolved.

desc:6810 U and desc:6809 F: I replaced the Cameron town-centroid locality for 'Cameron Jct' with OSM branch pole node/5211620240 (33.54637,-80.69793), named-facility, 500 m, confirmed. It sits where 46 kV way/623292013 joins way/12139895. Three plan mileages match it along OSM lines: 7.31 vs 7.3 mi to the Elloree tap, 9.9 vs 9.8 mi to St Matthews, and 7.81 vs 7.5 mi to Orangeburg #1. The old point was 2.0 km off.

desc:6809 F: I replaced the Orangeburg city-centroid locality for 'Orangeburg #1' with unnamed OSM way/185577980 (33.50331,-80.80766) at DESC's Orangeburg East complex (lower-confidence, 1000 m). It is the terminus of the 7.81 mi 46 kV line to Cameron Jct. The old point was 4.6 km west, in the wrong part of town.

desc:6809 G: I downgraded Hooks from confirmed to lower-confidence and widened uncertainty from 500 to 1000 m. The OSM feature is named 'GPC <-> SCG&E Compensator Station', not Hooks. Overpass topology shows it is the SCE&G/GPC ownership boundary on a 1.0 km spur off the Stevens Creek-McCormick 115/46 kV corridor. Plan mileages (Stevens Creek-Hooks 9.5, Hooks-Modoc 6.5, Hooks-Thurmond 2.3) fit this station or the corridor junction 0.98 km east about equally. I also noted that the 6809 G title was 'Stevens Creek - Hooks 115kV/LR Plumb Branch 46kV' in the 2024-2028 plan.

desc:6809 M: I flagged, but did not change, a key collision. Project ID '6809 M' appears twice in desc-scrtp-2026-2030, on p19 in this batch and on p48 (Modoc-McCormick) in batch desc-3, so both emit key 'desc:6809 M'.

desc:6809 M: I added OSM topology validation for both terminals: the continuous 230 kV path St George switching station (way/185032932) to Santee (way/185032971) to a junction at 33.8114,-80.3647 (way/185032933) to Sumter Substation (double-circuit way/185032969). desc:6808 P: I added topology for Hopkins. Both Wateree 230 kV lines (way/769275562 and way/185227953) end at the unnamed 230/115 kV way/185227970, and the Westinghouse facility distance (0.72 km) was re-verified with Nominatim.

desc:6810 J: I kept Santee City as lower-confidence and added the along-line evidence: 7.13 mi from the Elloree tap (7.94 mi including the tap) against the plan's 8.35 mi, versus 8.87 or 9.67 mi to the alternative Santee transmission substation. The distances do not decide the match.
